lines.text: India's biggest weather network already exists.
Nobody noticed — because we call it Jio.
Weather in India is hyperlocal, but our data isn't.
About forty Doppler radars cover 3.3 million square kilometres.
Heat alone could cost India thirty-four million jobs by 2030 —
and when insurance exists, claims take months.
Here's the insight: rain weakens the signal between towers —
and that tells you exactly how hard it's raining.
Phone batteries, averaged across a city, track air temperature.
Every tower is a rain gauge. Every phone is a thermometer.
We don't build sensors. We become the sensor.
Meet JioMausam: a live, street-level weather map of India, built from network data.
On top of it, Mausam Kavach — insurance on your recharge for twenty-nine rupees a month.
When the network measures 45 degrees near you,
the payout lands in your JioPay wallet within hours.
No claim forms. No waiting.
One percent of Jio's users is five million policies — about 170 crore rupees a year.
Gig platforms and insurers buy the data.
And Reliance is customer zero: JioMart, New Energy and Jio itself.
Why only Reliance?
It owns every layer — the network, 500 million customers,
payments, insurance and retail — under one roof.
A ninety-day pilot in Vidarbha and Ahmedabad. Then a national map.
India will adapt to climate change by listening to the infrastructure it already has.
This is JioMausam. Different by design.
